sources.title: egy-names / Egyptian Names & Onomastic Intelligence Dataset (family-classified canonical entries; Egyptian name-chain corpus)
sources.romanization_convention: Use each original source name_en value paired to Arabic name_ar, explicitly role=f (family surname); preserve recorded Egyptian English transcription, not an independently generated transliteration.
sources.selection: First 500 distinct eligible source family-role entries in the publisher's corpus-ranking order; runtime sampling from selected 500 is uniform, with no retained frequencies.
sources.limitations: Corpus derives from Egyptian exam/student name chains; publisher states national all-governorate coverage, not independently verified. Role classification and English transliteration have not been individually manually audited; research only.
sources.expansion_selection: Preserve 500 original family-role source spellings verbatim. Append 2,500 distinct name_en entries with role=f and matching Arabic name_ar in this Egyptian name-chain corpus; prioritize independently published Egyptian 2019 surname spellings; deduplicate normalized Arabic originals. Do not generate romanizations or assign frequency weights.

sources.title: Country EG 2019 surname-directory corroboration, Surname Dispersion Dataset (locatefamily.com crawl)
sources.license: MIT repository; upstream directory-data rights unverified
sources.romanization_convention: Preserve the primary empirical Egyptian corpus's English name_en spelling paired with original name_ar; the secondary country's Latin strings only corroborate spelling, never derive new Latin names.
sources.selection: Prefer family-role source values also present in Egyptian 2019 surname records, then use uncorroborated explicit family-role source entries. Frequency and percentages never retained; uniform sampling.
sources.limitations: Role=f is a publisher-assigned surname label from Egyptian name chains, not independently verified individuals' hereditary surnames. Geographic incidence, spelling consistency and reuse rights still require human audit.
